paper_metadata.title: QUANTUM MACHINE LEARNING ON NEAR-TERM QUANTUM DEVICES: CURRENT STATE OF SUPERVISED AND UNSUPERVISED TECHNIQUES FOR REAL-WORLD APPLICATIONS

summary: The paper is a survey of gate-based QML on real hardware, and in the finance section it highlights two concrete experiments: a 20-qubit IBM Quantum feature-selection study using a variational quantum algorithm with QN-SPSA, and a 5-qubit IBM Quantum qPCA study for pricing interest-rate derivatives from 2x2 and 3x3 cross-correlation matrices. The survey does not report quantitative classical-vs-quantum advantage for either finance experiment; it explicitly notes that the qPCA approach struggles to scale to larger datasets.

experiments.description: Quantum machine learning for financial feature selection using a variational quantum algorithm on IBM Quantum hardware.

algorithm.variant: Variational quantum algorithm for unconstrained black-box binary optimization applied to feature selection

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary feature-selection variables encoded as qubits in a black-box binary optimization formulation; exact mapping details not reported in the survey text.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Unconstrained black-box binary optimization for selecting a subset of features; exact mathematical objective not given in the survey text.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Unconstrained formulation; no explicit penalty terms reported in the survey text.

problem_instance.description: Feature selection for fraud detection in finance.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Reported as hardware results on IBM Quantum device; detailed validation protocol not given in the survey text.

speedup_claims.caveats: The survey text only states that the IBM Quantum device run on 20 qubits used QN-SPSA for feature selection and that hardware results were reported. It does not provide quantitative performance metrics, runtime, or a classical baseline for this finance experiment.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 20 qubits on IBM Quantum hardware; QN-SPSA optimization; no quantitative classical-vs-quantum benchmark reported in the survey text.
limiting_factors: No reported accuracy, runtime, or baseline comparison in the survey text
Feature-selection objective is described only qualitatively
NISQ hardware noise and limited qubit count
Data-loading and encoding overhead are not quantified

notes: The survey text identifies [135] as a finance application using a PQC with QN-SPSA on 20 qubits on IBM Quantum device.
Exact objective, ansatz, dataset, and runtime details are not provided in the survey text; only the experiment family and qubit count are explicit.
Speedup order is not characterized in the paper text, so set to none_proven.
The survey states that [135] used a PQC with QN-SPSA on 20 qubits on IBM Quantum device for feature selection, but it does not report a quantitative advantage claim.

experiments.description: Quantum principal component analysis for reducing noisy factors in pricing financial derivatives on IBM Quantum hardware.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Cross-correlation matrices of forward rates are processed via qPCA; exact qubit-to-variable mapping not reported in the survey text.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Low-rank approximation / principal component extraction of cross-correlation matrices for derivative pricing.

problem_instance.description: Pricing interest-rate financial derivatives using historical forward-rate data.

dataset_specification.description: 2×2 and 3×3 cross-correlation matrices based on historical data for two and three time-maturing forward rates.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Experiments performed on a 5-qubit IBM Quantum device; scaling to larger datasets discussed qualitatively.

speedup_claims.conditions: As described in the survey’s qPCA overview; the finance experiment itself is reported only qualitatively on a 5-qubit IBM Quantum device.
speedup_claims.caveats: The survey text does not report a measured speedup, accuracy, or runtime comparison for the financial derivative pricing experiment. It only notes that scaling to larger datasets was difficult.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 5-qubit IBM Quantum device; qPCA on 2x2 and 3x3 cross-correlation matrices.
limiting_factors: No measured classical baseline or speedup reported for the finance experiment
The survey only gives the asymptotic qPCA complexity O(log N)
Demonstration is on very small matrices (2x2 and 3x3)
Scaling to larger datasets is explicitly noted as difficult

notes: The survey text explicitly states that [205] used a 5-qubit IBM Quantum device for qPCA on 2×2 and 3×3 cross-correlation matrices.
The O(log N) complexity is taken from the qPCA description in the survey, not from a paper-specific benchmark.
No detailed optimizer, shots, or gate counts are reported in the survey text.
The survey reports qPCA on a 5-qubit IBM Quantum device for 2x2 and 3x3 cross-correlation matrices, but no experimental advantage over classical PCA is shown.
